notes.title: Weight memory rule of thumb
notes.body: Weight memory = parameters x bytes per parameter. FP32 = 4 B, FP16/BF16 = 2 B, INT8 = 1 B, INT4 = 0.5 B. A 7B model in FP16 needs about 14 GB just for weights; add KV cache and runtime overhead for inference.

notes.title: Training compute rule of thumb
notes.body: Training FLOPs are approximately 6 x N x D, where N = parameters and D = training tokens. Chinchilla suggests about 20 tokens per parameter for compute-optimal training.

notes.title: Why decoding is memory-bound
notes.body: At small batch sizes each generated token needs all weights read from memory, but does little math per byte. Memory bandwidth (HBM), not peak FLOPs, usually limits tokens per second.

notes.title: Roofline model
notes.body: Arithmetic intensity = FLOPs / bytes moved. If it is above the hardware ratio (peak FLOPs / memory bandwidth) the work is compute-bound; below it, memory-bound. Large-batch training is usually compute-bound; small-batch decoding is memory-bound.

notes.title: Inference compute per token
notes.body: A forward pass costs about 2 x N FLOPs per token (N = parameters). Training costs about 6 x N per token because the backward pass is about twice the forward pass.

notes.title: KV cache size
notes.body: Per token, the KV cache stores a key and a value for every layer: about 2 x layers x (kv heads x head dim) x bytes per value. Multiply by context length and batch size. Grouped-query attention shrinks it by sharing KV heads.

notes.title: Workflows vs agents
notes.body: Workflows orchestrate LLMs and tools through predefined code paths (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization). Agents let the LLM dynamically direct its own steps and tool use. Start with the simplest option that works.

notes.title: PagedAttention and continuous batching
notes.body: vLLM stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks, like OS memory pages, which cuts fragmentation and allows more concurrent requests. Continuous batching adds new requests as soon as others finish instead of waiting for the whole batch.

notes.title: What context engineering is
notes.body: Context engineering is choosing everything that goes into the model's context at each step: system instructions, tool definitions, retrieved documents, memory and message history. Context is a finite budget, and quality drops as it fills (context rot), so aim for the smallest set of high-signal tokens. Techniques: compaction (summarize history), structured note-taking outside the context, sub-agents with clean contexts, and just-in-time retrieval through tools.

notes.title: What an agent harness is
notes.body: The harness is the software around the model: it runs the agent loop (model -> tool call -> run tool -> feed result back), defines the tools, manages context and memory, enforces permissions and sandboxing, and decides when to stop. The same model can perform very differently in different harnesses. "Evaluation harness" means something else: a framework for running benchmarks against models, such as EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness.

notes.title: AI coding CLIs
notes.body: Terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider) read and edit files, run commands and tests, and use git. They load project instructions from files such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, ask permission for risky actions, and can run non-interactively in scripts and CI (for example claude -p "prompt").

questions.prompt: Which processor type is most commonly used to train large neural networks?
questions.explanation: GPUs offer massive parallel matrix-math throughput, which dominates neural network training.

questions.prompt: HBM stands for High Bandwidth Memory.
questions.explanation: HBM is stacked DRAM placed next to the accelerator die to provide very high memory bandwidth.

questions.prompt: Which NVIDIA interconnect provides high-bandwidth direct GPU-to-GPU communication?
questions.explanation: NVLink (and NVSwitch) gives far more GPU-to-GPU bandwidth than PCIe.

questions.prompt: What is Google's custom accelerator designed for machine learning called?
questions.explanation: The Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) is Google's ML ASIC. Gaudi is Intel's; Inferentia is AWS's.

questions.prompt: Name the 16-bit number format with 8 exponent bits and 7 mantissa bits widely used for training.
questions.explanation: bfloat16 keeps FP32's exponent range with fewer mantissa bits, which makes training stable at 16 bits.

questions.prompt: For LLM token generation at small batch sizes, performance is usually limited by:
questions.explanation: Each decode step reads all the weights but does little math per byte, so it is memory-bandwidth bound.

questions.prompt: Tensor Cores are specialized GPU units for matrix multiply-accumulate operations.
questions.explanation: Tensor Cores speed up mixed-precision matrix math (GEMMs), the core operation of deep learning.

questions.prompt: About how much memory do the weights of a 7B-parameter model take in FP16?
questions.explanation: 7B parameters x 2 bytes = 14 GB.

questions.prompt: About how much memory do the weights of a 70B model take when quantized to 4 bits?
questions.explanation: 70B x 0.5 bytes = 35 GB, before KV cache and overhead.

questions.prompt: How many bytes does one parameter take in FP32?
questions.explanation: 32 bits = 4 bytes.

questions.prompt: Which rule of thumb estimates transformer training compute (N = parameters, D = tokens)?
questions.explanation: About 2ND FLOPs for the forward pass and 4ND for the backward pass.

questions.prompt: KV cache memory grows linearly with context length and batch size.
questions.explanation: The KV cache stores keys and values per layer, per token and per sequence.

questions.prompt: Mixed-precision training with Adam needs roughly how many bytes per parameter for weights, gradients and optimizer states (excluding activations)?
questions.explanation: 2 (FP16 weights) + 2 (gradients) + 12 (FP32 master weights plus two Adam moments) = 16 bytes.

questions.prompt: Chinchilla scaling suggests compute-optimal training uses roughly how many tokens per parameter?
questions.explanation: Hoffmann et al. (2022) found about 20 tokens per parameter is compute-optimal.

questions.prompt: Which model family generates images by iteratively removing noise?
questions.explanation: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process.

questions.prompt: A GAN consists of a generator and a discriminator.
questions.explanation: The two networks are trained against each other.

questions.prompt: What does RAG stand for?
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant documents and adds them to the prompt to ground the answer.

questions.prompt: In generative AI, a 'hallucination' is:
options: Confident output not grounded in facts or the source
questions.answer: Confident output not grounded in facts or the source
questions.explanation: Models can produce fluent but false content.

questions.prompt: Raising the sampling temperature generally makes outputs:
questions.explanation: Higher temperature flattens the token probability distribution.

questions.prompt: VAEs are trained with a reconstruction loss plus a KL-divergence term on the latent distribution.
questions.explanation: This is the evidence lower bound (ELBO) objective.

questions.prompt: Which architecture underlies most modern LLMs?
questions.explanation: Introduced in 'Attention Is All You Need' (2017).

questions.prompt: What is the basic unit of text an LLM reads and generates called?
questions.explanation: Text is split into tokens (often subword pieces) by a tokenizer.

questions.prompt: Standard self-attention cost grows with sequence length n as:
questions.explanation: Every token attends to every other token.

questions.prompt: Decoder-only models like GPT are pretrained with a next-token prediction objective.
questions.explanation: Causal language modeling predicts each token from the tokens before it.

questions.prompt: What does RLHF stand for?
questions.explanation: RLHF aligns a model using a reward model trained on human preferences.

questions.prompt: How does LoRA fine-tune a model?
options: Adds trainable low-rank matrices while freezing the base weights
Retrains all weights at lower precision
questions.answer: Adds trainable low-rank matrices while freezing the base weights
questions.explanation: Only the small low-rank adapters are trained, which cuts memory and storage.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of positional encodings such as RoPE?
options: To give the model information about token order
questions.answer: To give the model information about token order
questions.explanation: Attention alone does not see order, so position information must be injected.

questions.prompt: In AI applications, embeddings are:
questions.explanation: Similar content maps to nearby vectors.

questions.prompt: Which type of database is optimized for similarity search over embeddings?
questions.explanation: Vector databases use approximate nearest-neighbour indexes such as HNSW.

questions.prompt: Prompt caching can reduce latency and cost when many requests share the same prompt prefix.
questions.explanation: The shared prefix is processed once and reused.

questions.prompt: Which metric measures the fraction of all relevant documents that appear in the top-k retrieved results?
questions.explanation: Precision@k is the fraction of the top-k results that are relevant.

questions.prompt: What is the technique called that lets an LLM call external functions or APIs through structured output?
questions.explanation: The model emits a structured call, the app runs it, and the result is fed back to the model.

questions.prompt: Why use chunk overlap when splitting documents for RAG?
options: To keep context that spans chunk boundaries
questions.answer: To keep context that spans chunk boundaries
questions.explanation: Overlap stops sentences or ideas from being cut in half.

questions.prompt: Which data split is kept aside for the final, unbiased evaluation?
questions.explanation: The validation set is used for tuning; the test set is touched only at the end.

questions.prompt: Overfitting means a model does well on its training data but poorly on new data.
questions.explanation: The model memorizes noise instead of learning patterns that generalize.

questions.prompt: Which optimizer is most commonly used to train transformers?
questions.explanation: AdamW is Adam with decoupled weight decay.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of learning-rate warmup?
questions.explanation: Starting with a small learning rate avoids large, unstable updates while the optimizer statistics settle.

questions.prompt: Data leakage happens when information from the test set influences training, which inflates scores.
questions.explanation: Leakage makes offline metrics look better than real-world performance.

questions.prompt: What does gradient (activation) checkpointing trade?
options: Extra compute for less activation memory
questions.answer: Extra compute for less activation memory
questions.explanation: Activations are recomputed during the backward pass instead of being stored.

questions.prompt: What is the technique called where a small model is trained to imitate a large model?
questions.explanation: The student learns from the teacher's outputs or logits.

questions.prompt: How does FlashAttention speed up attention?
options: By approximating attention with low-rank matrices
By tiling to cut reads and writes between HBM and on-chip SRAM
By running attention on the CPU
questions.answer: By tiling to cut reads and writes between HBM and on-chip SRAM
questions.explanation: It is IO-aware: it computes exact attention in tiles that fit in fast SRAM and never writes the full attention matrix to HBM.

questions.prompt: In the roofline model, an operation is compute-bound when its arithmetic intensity is ___ the hardware's FLOPs-per-byte ratio.
questions.explanation: Above the ridge point, memory keeps up and peak FLOPs is the limit.

questions.prompt: MLPerf is a suite of industry benchmarks for AI training and inference performance, run by MLCommons.
questions.explanation: MLPerf results are the standard way to compare AI hardware systems.

questions.prompt: NVIDIA's Transformer Engine, which uses FP8 precision, was first introduced with the Hopper (H100) architecture.
questions.explanation: Hopper introduced the Transformer Engine; Blackwell extended it to lower precisions such as FP4.

questions.prompt: In data-parallel training, what does ZeRO (as described in the Ultra-Scale Playbook) do?
options: Shards optimizer states, gradients and parameters across GPUs
Splits each layer across GPUs (tensor parallelism)
questions.answer: Shards optimizer states, gradients and parameters across GPUs
questions.explanation: Plain data parallelism replicates everything on each GPU; ZeRO partitions it to save memory.

questions.prompt: About how many FLOPs does an inference forward pass cost per token for a model with N parameters?
questions.explanation: Each parameter takes part in about one multiply and one add per token.

questions.prompt: The Kaplan et al. scaling laws found that language model loss scales with model size, data and compute as a:
questions.explanation: Loss falls smoothly as a power law in each factor when the others are not bottlenecks.

questions.prompt: Grouped-query attention (GQA) reduces KV cache memory by letting several query heads share the same key/value heads.
questions.explanation: Fewer KV heads means proportionally less KV cache per token.

questions.prompt: When sizing GPU memory for LLM serving, what usually grows with the number of concurrent users and the context length?
questions.explanation: Weights are fixed; the KV cache scales with tokens in flight.

questions.prompt: The InstructGPT paper reported that outputs from a 1.3B-parameter InstructGPT model were preferred by human raters over the 175B GPT-3.
questions.explanation: Alignment with RLHF mattered more than raw size for following instructions.

questions.prompt: What tokenization algorithm, used by GPT models, repeatedly merges the most frequent pair of symbols?
questions.explanation: BPE builds a subword vocabulary by iteratively merging frequent pairs.

questions.prompt: Why do transformers use multi-head attention instead of a single attention head?
options: To attend to information from different representation subspaces at once
questions.answer: To attend to information from different representation subspaces at once
questions.explanation: Each head can learn different relationships, such as syntax or coreference.

questions.prompt: In Karpathy's Zero to Hero series, what is the name of the tiny autograd engine built in the first lecture?
questions.explanation: micrograd implements backpropagation over a scalar computation graph.

questions.prompt: Which organization developed the ALLaM Arabic-English language models?
questions.explanation: ALLaM is described in arXiv 2407.15390.

questions.prompt: Jais is an Arabic-centric open generative LLM developed by Inception (G42), MBZUAI and Cerebras.
questions.explanation: Jais and Jais-chat are described in arXiv 2308.16149.

questions.prompt: Latent diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion) run the diffusion process in the compressed latent space of an autoencoder rather than directly on pixels.
questions.explanation: Working in latent space makes high-resolution generation much cheaper.

questions.prompt: What does classifier-free guidance do in a text-to-image diffusion model?
options: Removes the need for a text encoder
Pushes generations to follow the prompt more closely
Speeds up sampling by skipping steps
questions.answer: Pushes generations to follow the prompt more closely
questions.explanation: It mixes conditional and unconditional predictions; a higher guidance scale means stronger prompt adherence, often with less diversity.

questions.prompt: Which technique gives a model a few worked examples inside the prompt?
questions.explanation: The examples show the expected format and behavior without any training.

questions.prompt: According to Anthropic's "Building Effective Agents", what distinguishes an agent from a workflow?
options: An agent always uses multiple models
An agent lets the LLM dynamically direct its own process and tool use
An agent never needs a prompt
questions.answer: An agent lets the LLM dynamically direct its own process and tool use
questions.explanation: Workflows follow predefined code paths; agents decide their own steps.

questions.prompt: What problem does vLLM's PagedAttention solve?
options: Wasted memory and fragmentation in the KV cache
questions.answer: Wasted memory and fragmentation in the KV cache
questions.explanation: It allocates the KV cache in blocks like OS memory pages, so more requests fit in memory.

questions.prompt: Continuous batching improves serving throughput by adding new requests to the running batch as soon as others finish.
questions.explanation: Static batching waits for the slowest sequence; continuous batching keeps the GPU busy.

questions.prompt: Indirect prompt injection happens when malicious instructions arrive through content the model reads, such as retrieved documents or emails.
questions.explanation: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data and defend at the model, prompt and system level.

questions.prompt: Which LLM-system pattern validates and filters model outputs (for example, schema checks or safety filters) before they reach users?
questions.explanation: Guardrails are a core pattern alongside evals, RAG, caching and defensive UX.

questions.prompt: Rule #1 of Google's Rules of ML is: do not be afraid to launch a product without machine learning.
questions.explanation: Heuristics can get a product working; add ML once you have data.

questions.prompt: In PyTorch, which method do you call on the loss tensor to compute gradients?
questions.explanation: autograd fills .grad on every tensor that has requires_grad=True.

questions.prompt: Starting from a pretrained model and adapting it to a new task is called:
questions.explanation: It needs far less data and compute than training from scratch.

questions.prompt: Which company develops the Llama family of open-weight models?
questions.explanation: Llama models are released by Meta AI.

questions.prompt: Which lab develops the Gemini models?
questions.explanation: Gemini is Google DeepMind's multimodal model family.

questions.prompt: Which company develops the Claude models?
questions.explanation: Claude is built by Anthropic.

questions.prompt: The Qwen open model family comes from which company?
questions.explanation: Qwen is developed by Alibaba Cloud.

questions.prompt: What is context engineering?
options: Curating everything the model sees at each step: instructions, tools, data and history
Training a model on longer documents
Increasing the context window size in hardware
questions.answer: Curating everything the model sees at each step: instructions, tools, data and history
questions.explanation: It goes beyond writing one prompt: it manages the whole context window over a multi-step task.

questions.prompt: The "Lost in the Middle" paper found that LLMs use information best when it is placed:
options: At the beginning or end of the context
questions.answer: At the beginning or end of the context
questions.explanation: Accuracy drops for relevant facts buried in the middle of a long context.

questions.prompt: "Context rot" refers to model performance degrading as the amount of input in the context grows.
questions.explanation: Longer contexts are not free: recall and reasoning get worse as tokens accumulate.

questions.prompt: When an agent nears its context limit, what does compaction do?
options: Summarizes the history and continues in a fresh context with that summary
questions.answer: Summarizes the history and continues in a fresh context with that summary
questions.explanation: Compaction keeps key decisions and state while dropping redundant tool output.

questions.prompt: In just-in-time retrieval, an agent keeps lightweight references (like file paths) and loads the data with tools only when needed.
questions.explanation: This avoids filling the context with data up front.

questions.prompt: Why does the Manus team advise keeping the prompt prefix stable and the context append-only?
options: To maximize the KV-cache hit rate, which cuts latency and cost
To make the model forget old tools
questions.answer: To maximize the KV-cache hit rate, which cuts latency and cost
questions.explanation: Any change early in the prompt invalidates the cached prefix for everything after it.

questions.prompt: Which failure is it when a hallucination or error enters the context and is then repeatedly referenced?
questions.explanation: Drew Breunig lists poisoning, distraction, confusion and clash as the ways long contexts fail.

questions.prompt: Using sub-agents with their own clean context windows can keep the main agent's context focused.
questions.explanation: Sub-agents explore deeply and return only a condensed result.

questions.prompt: In AI agents, what is the "harness"?
options: The software around the model that runs the loop, tools, context and permissions
questions.answer: The software around the model that runs the loop, tools, context and permissions
questions.explanation: The model decides; the harness executes tool calls, manages state and enforces limits.

questions.prompt: A basic agent loop is: the model requests a tool call, the harness runs it, the result is added to the context, and this repeats until the task is done.
questions.explanation: This loop is the core of most agent harnesses.

questions.prompt: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
options: An open protocol for connecting AI applications to tools and data sources
questions.answer: An open protocol for connecting AI applications to tools and data sources
questions.explanation: MCP standardizes how hosts discover and call tools, resources and prompts from servers.

questions.prompt: What is EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness used for?
options: Running standard benchmarks against language models
questions.answer: Running standard benchmarks against language models
questions.explanation: An evaluation harness is a different meaning of "harness" from an agent harness.

questions.prompt: What does SWE-bench measure?
options: Whether a system can resolve real GitHub issues so that the tests pass
questions.answer: Whether a system can resolve real GitHub issues so that the tests pass
questions.explanation: Tasks come from real open-source repositories, checked by their unit tests.

questions.prompt: Sandboxing in an agent harness (restricting file system and network access) limits the damage a wrong or manipulated agent action can do.
questions.explanation: Permissions and sandboxes are the main safety layer around tool execution.

questions.prompt: For agents that work across many context windows, what does Anthropic recommend the harness keep outside the context?
options: Progress notes and state files (plus git history) that the next session reads
The full raw transcript pasted into every prompt
Nothing: start each session from scratch
questions.answer: Progress notes and state files (plus git history) that the next session reads
questions.explanation: A fresh session can pick up where the last one stopped by reading persistent artifacts.

questions.prompt: Which company makes Claude Code, an agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal?
questions.explanation: Claude Code reads code, edits files and runs commands.

questions.prompt: Codex CLI, an open-source terminal coding agent, comes from which company?
questions.explanation: Its source is on GitHub at openai/codex.

questions.prompt: Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent from Google that runs in the terminal.
questions.explanation: Its source is on GitHub at google-gemini/gemini-cli.

questions.prompt: What file in a project root does Claude Code read for project instructions and memory?
questions.explanation: It holds commands, conventions and context the agent should always know.

questions.prompt: What is AGENTS.md?
options: An open format file that gives coding agents project instructions
questions.answer: An open format file that gives coding agents project instructions
questions.explanation: Several coding agents read it, like a README written for agents.

questions.prompt: Which Claude Code flag runs a single prompt non-interactively, prints the result and exits (useful in scripts and CI)?
questions.explanation: For example: claude -p "explain this project".

questions.prompt: Aider is an open-source AI pair-programming tool that works in the terminal with your git repository.
questions.explanation: Aider edits files and commits changes with descriptive messages.
